new_entities.name: School-based obesity intervention
new_entities.description: A school-delivered intervention targeting diet, physical activity, or the broader school environment to prevent or reduce childhood or adolescent obesity.

new_entities.name: BMI z score
new_entities.description: Age- and sex-standardized BMI expressed as a z score in children or adolescents.

edges.effect_quant: A 2021 meta-analysis of 14 adolescent studies found a small favorable intervention effect on BMI z score of -0.06 (95% CI -0.10 to -0.03), and a broader 2013 meta-analysis of 32 randomized trials involving 52,109 participants found school-based obesity prevention programs mildly effective overall.
edges.population: school-aged children and adolescents exposed to school-based obesity prevention or reduction programs
edges.mechanism: School interventions may improve diet quality, reduce sugary or high-energy intake, increase physical activity, and shift the everyday food and activity environment across the school day.
edges.summary: School-based obesity interventions produce small but real improvements in BMI z score overall, especially when they are multi-component and sustained rather than brief or purely informational.
edges.caveats: Effects are modest and inconsistent across age groups, with weaker impacts often seen in older adolescents. Many interventions require environmental change, parental involvement, or longer follow-up to produce durable anthropometric differences.

evidence.citation: Salgado-Figueroa A et al 2021 Int J Behav Nutr Phys Act
evidence.notes: A systematic review and meta-analysis of school-based interventions with health education to reduce body mass index in adolescents aged 10 to 19 years.

evidence.citation: Sobol-Goldberg S et al 2013 Obesity (Silver Spring)
evidence.notes: School-based obesity prevention programs: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
